body:
The first navmesh may "look nice" but is very inefficient and broken for pathfinding. It is the complete opposite of why games want to use navmesh in the first place. At that point you might as well switch to use grid-based pathfinding instead of a navmesh for a better result.

The second navmesh is just a matter of finding bake settings that somehow make sense for the used geometry. In general over-detailed terrain meshes yield low quality baked navmesh. They are just too noisy geometry that causes many mini polygons which are both bad for quality and performance.

Apart from that I don't know what to tell you but having "geometry beauty" and being super accurate are both highly, if not completely irrelevant criteria for a navmesh. A navmesh is always an abstraction that ideally has as little detail as possible. That it does not align close to the terrain geometry or any other ground geometry is very much expected. A navmesh hovers above or goes below the geometry so you need to do your actual actor ground alignment with something else anyway.

You not knowing this and thinking that the first navmesh is the navmesh that you want and need for a game tells me that you have little experience with navmesh. You should check out some general infos on the internet around navmesh and its use in video games to better manage your expectations, else your "geometry beauty obsession" will likely give you endless frustrations.

It seems like you got stuck on some of the words I used here. I should clarify. When I say the low poly navmesh is terrible, thats because it is. That low poly mesh does not work for even basic pathfinding. Agents get stuck, they freeze, they take long inefficient routes. The pathfinding on the high poly model works just as you would expect it. 

If you reread the post carefully you'll see that I added a screenshot that shows a player of 2m can fit entirely under the navmesh. If an agent tried to find a path to that player it would fail, as that point is 4-5 meters under the generated navmesh.

You not knowing that a navmesh going through the floor or floating 5 meters above the floor causes issues with pathfinding tells me that you have little experience with navmeshes. From the docs : "A navigation mesh is a collection of polygons that define which areas of an environment are traversable to aid agents in pathfinding through complicated spaces." 
Would you consider areas under the map or floating above the map to be traversable areas?

A good amount of community people already invested their time on you trying to help you in other places but you discarded all their help and correct knowledge. Now you went through places to end here hoping for a better outcome that you can not get.

Closing as this gets us nowhere.
